edits.old: For Atlas Core multi-cloud deployments, MongoDB documents that an application using a private connection to a replica set can access only nodes in the same cloud provider and region. To reach nodes in other providers, Atlas requires a VPN from the current provider to each remaining provider and an Atlas private endpoint for each. Atlas also describes a sharded alternative: applications connect through local private endpoints, and local mongos routes requests to a primary in another region. The MongoDB Server Discovery and Monitoring specification requires replica-set clients to discover and monitor the full set from a seed list of one or more members, and requires the member hostnames in the replica-set configuration to be reachable from the client. A Reddit commenter reports an AWS/GCP deployment that used cloud-specific mongos seed lists for its sharded topology and says replica-set clients still tried all members when given single-cloud seed hosts. Treat the forum account as a topology-specific report to validate against the exact deployment. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24)
edits.new: For Atlas Core multi-cloud deployments, MongoDB documents that an application using a private connection to a replica set can access only nodes in the same cloud provider and region. To reach nodes in other providers, Atlas requires a VPN from the current provider to each remaining provider and an Atlas private endpoint for each. Atlas also describes a sharded alternative: applications connect through local private endpoints, and the local mongos routes requests to a primary in another region. The MongoDB Server Discovery and Monitoring specification requires clients to discover an entire replica set from a seed list of one or more members, and requires replica set members to be reachable from the client by the hostnames listed in the replica set config. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-config/multi-cloud-distribution.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-discovery-and-monitoring.md

edits.new: Write latency depends on the distance between the application, the primary and the other cluster nodes, and on the replication needed for the requested write concern. A w: "majority" write is acknowledged only after a majority of voting, data-bearing nodes have the write, so a higher write concern increases write latency. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/latency-strategies/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern.md
